scope: Theorem 4.1 (Index inequality along calibrated paths) of the manuscript “Gigli’s distributional curvature characterization of Alexandrov spaces” (preprints/Giglis-distributional-curvature-characterization-of-Alexandrov-spaces-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 356 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e104c43128bea292), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 24. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let n ≥ 2 be an integer and let (M, d, m), with m = Hn, be a full-support RCD((n − 1)κ, n) space satisfying (1.4) for every global X, Y ∈ TestV(M) and every nonnegative f ∈ Test(M). Let u be bounded globally Lipschitz and constant outside a compact set, and let Φt = Qtu. There is a Borel prescription S : x 7→ S(x) ∈ Geo(M), defined outside one m-null set, with S(x)1 = x and S(x) satisfying (4.2). For every nonnegative compactly supported Lipschitz f, write πf = S#(fm), with forward velocity v. The plan has terminal measure fm, uniformly bounded speed, and bounded compression on every [δ, 1], δ > 0. Let Z be a compactly supported test gradient. For every 0 < δ < 1 and every trial (4.1) with the global endpoint identities Yδ = 0 and Y1 = Z, one has HΦ1 (Z, Z)(f) ≤ Z Geo(M) Z 1 δ  |∂tY + ∇vY |2 − κ|Y ∧ v|2  (γt) dt dπf (γ). (4.3) The left side is the distributional evaluation (2.4); the right side is finite. Neither the path prescription nor its velocity depends on the choice of Z, the trial, or the terminal density.
